title: Kissed Kenyan Fish Stew
description: A sour, tender lazy‑Sunday stew with semolina and deglaze, perfect for a pescatarian feast.
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger; sauté until onion is translucent.
Stir in tomato paste and diced tomatoes, cooking for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Sprinkle in curry powder, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; stir for 30 seconds to bloom the spices.
Pour in vegetable broth and bring to a gentle simmer, letting the flavors meld for 10 minutes.
Add the fish fillets, cover, and simmer for 8 minutes until the fish is opaque and tender.
While the fish cooks, whisk semolina with a small amount of cold water to make a smooth slurry.
Deglaze the pot with lemon juice, then stir in the semolina slurry, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Cook for an additional 2 minutes until the sauce thickens, then garnish with chopped coriander before serving.
